name: Bishop's Bridge
connectingPointsDisplay: rail approaches to Paddington station — Paddington Arm of Grand Union Canal
facts: Bishop's Bridge, originally designed by Isambard Kingdom Brunel in 1839, was the first iron bridge to use bulb‑headed cast iron girders, a design that later inspired his famed balloon‑flange girders.

In 2003, English Heritage inspector Steven Brindle uncovered the forgotten canal section of Brunel's bridge, leading to its dismantling in 2004 and a 2006 plan to reconstruct it 180 metres downstream.

The modern replacement, built by Hochtief and opened on 14 June 2006, spans the rail approaches to Paddington station and the Paddington Arm of the Grand Union Canal, preserving the route’s historic flow.
